description: §19.9.9 body split × §19.8.3 (RUNTIME, sqlEngine:"real"): `addNote()` runs a HANDLED write `?{INSERT …}.run() !{ _ :> {} }` and then writes `@status`. It splits exactly as the unhandled form does — the INSERT runs on the server, `@status` lands on the client ("added"), and a later read sees the new row (n=2). Pre-S455 (g-impl1-handled-sql-lowering-defects-s455 item 9) the guard hid the query from the split classifier: the statement was tiered CLIENT, the function was not split, and the cell write raised E-RI-002.
rationale: §19.9.9.1: a statement is `server` tier when it holds its own `?{}` SQL; §19.8.3: a `!{}` handler on the query adds a failure path and changes nothing else about the statement it handles.
